title: adjudications
description: harness/adjudications.json: verdicts on specific outputs of specific corpus sentences, or on an input's grammaticality. The citation names the split and the line ('dev 17: the sentence .'), exactly as the baseline keys it; check_schemas verifies it against the pinned corpus.

verdict.description: right: natural Japanese that says what the English says, plain or polite; stiff: grammatical and faithful but not how it is said; wrong: the meaning is lost or changed, a form or particle is ungrammatical, the giving or receiving verb points the wrong way, or the plain or polite form contradicts a clue in the sentence; input_ungrammatical: the corpus line's English is not standard

output.description: the exact output judged (required for right / stiff / wrong)

cause.description: what a stiff or wrong verdict blames (required for both): sense — a word's wrong sense or choice; preposition — a preposition's wrong particle or sense; idiom — a multiword expression or construction read word for word; case — the wrong particle on a verb's argument; giving — the direction of あげる / くれる / もらう; structure — attachment, scope or clause structure misread; tense — tense, aspect or modality; morphology — an ill-formed Japanese form; it — a dummy or deictic it / there; quantity — number, quantifier, determiner or degree; negation — polarity; pronoun — a pronoun or possessive, wrong or redundant; register — plain or polite against a clue in the sentence; omission — a content word dropped; literal — a literal wording where Japanese has a set one; order — word order

judge.description: who gave the verdict; absent on the verdicts recorded before the field existed
